title: Pain During Urination
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with dysuria, urinary frequency, urgency, suprapubic pain, and no vaginal discharge or irritation. No systemic symptoms (fever, CVA tenderness → rules out pyelo). Uncomplicated UTI in healthy premenopausal non-pregnant woman. Most common: E. coli (80%). Diagnosis: UA — positive leukocyte esterase, nitrites, pyuria, bacteriuria. Urine culture not routinely needed for uncomplicated cystitis (treat empirically). Treatment: nitrofurantoin 100mg PO BID x 5d (first-line), TMP-SMX DS PO BID x 3d (if local resistance <20%), fosfomycin 3g PO once. Avoid fluoroquinolones for uncomplicated cystitis (FDA warnings). Counsel: void after intercourse, adequate hydration, cranberry products (limited evidence). If recurrent → postcoital or continuous prophylaxis.
